newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: KLASCO FALLS AS SLEEPY BOURSE EXTENDS LOSSES.
newsitem.headline: KLASCO FALLS AS SLEEPY BOURSE EXTENDS LOSSES.

text.p: Lithuania's sleepy market continued to see losses on Wednesday and dealers said that it would not shake from its slumber for awhile.

Dealers are pinning their hopes on foreign investors, who they hope will soon be lured to the market by low prices, improved company performances, a stronger banking sector and the sale of key state assets.

They also hope that a bourse decision to lift limits on block trade price flucuations will lead to increased activity on the market, which has struggled to regain the momentum it had during a brief bull-run in January.
But the short-term prospects looked bleak, dealers said.
"Nothing interesting is going to happen soon," said one dealer.
The session's biggest loser was state-run KLASCO, the largest stevedoring company in the country, which eased ten percent for the second straight day, falling to 13.77 litas from 15.30 litas.

"The fall was caused by the decision of the company's shareholders...to double the share capital of the company from reserves which will lead to an increased number of shares on the market," said Grazhina Bachiuliene, a dealer with Vifima.
Lithuanian Gas bounced back as anticipated, rising to 1.90 litas from 1.82 litas in light trade of almost 4,400 litas.
Dealers said that demand for the state-run gas firm was high as it looked like a bargain and few investors wanted to part with their shares at such a low price.
On the central market, Birzai Dairy was the most traded stock, turning over 133,000 litas. Its price advanced 2.30 percent to 10.25 litas.
Hermis Bank shares were also in relative demand, with almost 114,000 litas worth of them swapping hands at the unchanged price of 175.00 litas.
